## Fourth-order, cell/face-consistent density reference (`SNAP_WB_REF4`) {#sec-ch05-wbref4}

### Summary

The kernel's density reference is second order: the binomial smoothing biases $\chi=\rho/p$ by $\tfrac{\Delta x_1^2}{2}\partial_1^2\chi$,
and its face density is not the face value of its own cell density, so the solver's face density carries the
offset @eq-ch05-refkernel-offset. That offset enters the $x_1$ mass flux at linear order and, through it, the gravity work. The
switch removes it with two operators: a five-point filter with zero second and third moments, which keeps the
reference fourth order while still removing the two-cell mode, and a face value taken from the quartic through the
primitive of the cell reference, so that face and cell are consistent by construction. On a non-uniform grid it also
replaces the log-mean cell pressure by the average of a cubic through four face pressures.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Makes the reference density fourth order and its face value consistent with its cell value, @eq-ch05-wbref4-dref.

**Data.** Reads $\chi$, $p_{\mathrm{ref}}$ and $p_{\mathrm{sf}}$ of the kernel; replaces $\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}$ and $\rho_{\mathrm{sf}}$.

**Placement.** Inside `HydroImpl::_hydro_ref_x1`: cells before the seam exchange, faces after it.

**Activation.** Environment variable `SNAP_WB_REF4` (or `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT`), default off; needs $n_g\ge3$.

**Guarantee / limits.** $\eta_{\rho,f}=O(\Delta x_1^4)$ where no guard fires; $p_{\mathrm{sf}}$ and so the rest balance are unchanged.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer below, @tbl-ch05-wbref4-tests.
:::

Local symbols: $\mathsf F$ [-] the five-point filter; $\Pi$ [kg m$^{-2}$] the primitive of the cell reference
density; $i_0$ the first cell of a stencil window, $l$ the cell offset in it and $l_{\mathrm f}$ the face offset; $\ell_{l_{\mathrm f}}$
the Lagrange basis polynomial of face $i_0+l_{\mathrm f}$; $\tilde p$ [Pa] the cubic through four face pressures; $\zeta$ a
Gauss-Legendre node; $n_{\mathrm{poly}}$ the polytropic index and $\mathcal S_i$ [J kg$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$ s$^{-1}$] the entropy
tendency of cell $i$, both in the order test. $\vartheta$[^rg-3739b5b2fec3], $\lambda_w$[^rg-cf66429c8e8b], $\chi$, $\eta_{\rho,f}$, $\mathcal W$, $\Delta x_1$, $n_g$ and $\epsilon_{\mathrm m}$ are defined in @sec-appa
or @sec-ch05-refkernel.

Guards keep the kernel's values wherever the new ones would leave the local range or the column is under-resolved,
and the cell part runs before the seam exchange of @sec-ch05-seam, the face part after it. With the corrected-PE[^rg-36523dc32e4e] face
work of @sec-ch06 on (its default with `gravity-work: face`), the one-step spurious stratification of a neutral column
converges at about fourth order with the switch and second order without it.

*Aliases.* "Leg W" in the centroid derivation note; `SNAPY_WB_REF_EXACT` in the specification.[^ch05-wb4-alias]

[^ch05-wb4-alias]: `docs/derivations/x1-centroid-spherical.md`; `sources/gw__NEXTPR_spec_wbref_exact.md`.

### Derivation

Notation as in @sec-ch05-refkernel; indices are cell indices and $\chi_i=\overline\rho_i/\overline p_i$. The derivation is
that of the derivation note,[^ch05-wb4-note] re-written here and checked by `[C3]`, `[C7]`, `[C8]`, `[C14]`.

[^ch05-wb4-note]: `docs/derivations/wb-ref4.md@c0c38593d3d3f37bebe204a590610fd7daa05a5f` §§2-7.

#### Cell density

$$
\begin{aligned}
\rho_{\mathrm{ref},i} &= p_{\mathrm{ref},i}\,(\mathsf F\chi)_i, \\
\mathsf F &= \tfrac1{16}(-1,\,4,\,10,\,4,\,-1).
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch05-wbref4-dref}

$\mathsf F$ has unit sum, zero first, second and third moments and fourth moment $-\tfrac32$ in cell units, and zero response
to the two-cell mode, wavelength $\lambda_w=2\Delta x_1$ ($\vartheta=\pi/2$) (`[C3]`), so $\mathsf F\chi=\chi+O(\Delta x_1^4)$ for smooth $\chi$ and the two-cell mode is still removed; its reach, $\pm2$, is
the binomial's, so ghost depth and seam exchange are unchanged. With $p_{\mathrm{ref}}=\overline p+c+O(\Delta x_1^6)$
(@sec-ch05-refkernel) the cell reference is $\overline\rho+c\chi+O(\Delta x_1^4)$, and the smooth $c\chi$ is carried
consistently by the face value below. @eq-ch05-wbref4-dref is built in `wb_ref4_stencils` as the filter row `F` ($\mathsf F$)
({{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_stencils >}})
and applied in `wb_ref4_cells` as `fr`
({{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_cells >}}).

At a clamped wall the two values past the wall are cubic extrapolations of the four owned cells nearest it,
$\chi_0..\chi_3$ counted from the wall:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\chi_{-1} &= 4\chi_0 - 6\chi_1 + 4\chi_2 - \chi_3, \\
\chi_{-2} &= 10\chi_0 - 20\chi_1 + 15\chi_2 - 4\chi_3 .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch05-wbref4-cubic}

All five stencil values of the first two cells then lie on one cubic, which $\mathsf F$ reproduces, so $(\mathsf F\chi)_0=\chi_0$ and
$(\mathsf F\chi)_1=\chi_1$ for any data (`[C7]`): filtering with these wall values and leaving the two end cells unfiltered are the
same reference. Ghosts are never read.

#### Face density

$$
\begin{aligned}
\rho_{\mathrm{sf},f} &= \partial_1 \Pi(x_{1,f}), \\
\Pi(x_{1,i_0+l_{\mathrm f}}) &= \sum_{l<l_{\mathrm f}}\rho_{\mathrm{ref},i_0+l}\,\Delta x_{1,i_0+l},
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch05-wbref4-face}

with $\Pi$ the quartic through the primitive at the five faces $l_{\mathrm f}=0..4$ (four cells), window $i_0=f-2$ kept inside the owned cells at a
clamped wall, physical spacing. On a uniform grid of width $\Delta x_1$, $\Pi$ takes the values $0,\ \Delta x_1\rho_{\mathrm{ref},i_0},\ \Delta x_1(\rho_{\mathrm{ref},i_0}+\rho_{\mathrm{ref},i_0+1}),\dots$
at the faces $l_{\mathrm f}=0..4$; writing $\Pi$ in the Lagrange basis $\ell_{l_{\mathrm f}}$ of those five faces and differentiating,
$\rho_{\mathrm{sf},i_0+l_{\mathrm f}}=\partial_1\Pi(x_{1,i_0+l_{\mathrm f}})=\sum_{l=0}^{3}\rho_{\mathrm{ref},i_0+l}\,\Delta x_1\sum_{l'_{\mathrm f}>l}\partial_1\ell_{l'_{\mathrm f}}(x_{1,i_0+l_{\mathrm f}})$, which on
$\rho_{\mathrm{ref},i_0..i_0+3}$ is $(25,-23,13,-3)/12$ at $l_{\mathrm f}=0$ (the wall face), $(3,13,-5,1)/12$ at $l_{\mathrm f}=1$ (the next) and
$(-1,7,7,-1)/12$ at $l_{\mathrm f}=2$ (the interior face, window $i_0=f-2$) (`[C8]`). The face is exact for cubic
point profiles on any grid, so $\eta_{\rho,f}=\rho_{\mathrm{sf}}-\mathcal W[\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}]=O(\Delta x_1^4)$ (`[C14]`:
mid-column offset $3.22\times10^{-12}$, $5.18\times10^{-14}$, $6.91\times10^{-16}$ relative at $n_1$ = 32, 64, 128, orders
5.96 and 6.23, against order 2.00 for the kernel; at $n_1=256$ it is at round-off level, $1.38\times10^{-16}$ in this run, so
that level measures round-off, not truncation). @eq-ch05-wbref4-face is built as the weights `awt`
({{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_stencils >}})
and applied by `wb_ref4_faces`
({{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_faces >}}).

#### Non-uniform cell pressure

On a non-uniform grid the cell pressure becomes the cell average of the cubic $\tilde p$ through the face pressures at
faces $i-1..i+2$ (window inside the owned faces at a clamped wall), by three-point Gauss-Legendre, exact for a cubic:

$$
p_{\mathrm{ref},i} = \frac{1}{\Delta x_{1,i}}\int_{x_{1,i-1/2}}^{x_{1,i+1/2}}\tilde p\,\mathrm{d}x_1
= \tfrac{5}{18}\,\tilde p\big(x_{1,i}-\zeta\tfrac{\Delta x_{1,i}}{2}\big)+\tfrac{8}{18}\,\tilde p(x_{1,i})
+\tfrac{5}{18}\,\tilde p\big(x_{1,i}+\zeta\tfrac{\Delta x_{1,i}}{2}\big),
$$ {#eq-ch05-wbref4-pnu}

with $\zeta=\sqrt{3/5}$, the non-uniform branch of `wb_ref4_stencils` with the Gauss weights `gw`
({{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_stencils >}}).
A value outside the cell's two face pressures keeps the log-mean. This moves the discrete fixed point of a non-uniform
column by $O(\Delta x_1^2)$, so `balance_column` iterates against it (@sec-ch05-balcol). On a uniform grid the
six-face $p_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is kept.

#### Guards and rest balance

A cell whose $(\mathsf F\chi)_i$ lies outside $[\min,\max]$ of $\chi$ over cells $i-1..i+1$, with relative margin $10^{-10}$, keeps the
kernel's ratio; a face outside its two neighbouring cell references keeps the kernel's face. A cell with
$\lvert\ln(p_{\mathrm{sf},i-1/2}/p_{\mathrm{sf},i+1/2})\rvert>0.5$, fewer than two cells per pressure scale height, is
flagged, the flag is dilated by two cells, and flagged cells and faces next to them keep the kernel's values; ghosts
past a clamped wall do not count. The flag reads $p_{\mathrm{sf}}$ at most three cells away, which is why $n_g\ge3$ is
required: then both sides of an $x_1$ seam compute the same flag. The threshold, dilation and margin are design
choices, not derived. Since $p_{\mathrm{sf}}$ is never changed and on a uniform grid neither is $p_{\mathrm{ref}}$, the
rest state @eq-ch05-wbx1-rest is the kernel's.

*Why the two sides of an $x_1$ seam agree.* Four steps.

1. *The cell part runs before the exchange.* `wb_ref4_cells` is called before `pass_x1_anchor`, so the ghost rows a
   neighbour receives already hold the replaced $\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}$.
2. *The face part reads only exchanged cells.* `wb_ref4_faces` runs after the exchange, and its four-cell window at an
   interior face reaches two cells past the face, inside $n_g\ge2$.
3. *The flag reads three cells.* The flag of a cell uses its own $p_{\mathrm{sf}}$ ratio, dilated by two cells
   (`max_pool1d` of width 5), so a face next to a seam depends on scan pressures up to three cells away. With $n_g\ge3$
   both blocks hold them, which is the setup check.
4. *The guards do not flip on round-off.* `in_range` widens each bound by `kMargin` $=10^{-10}$ relative, far above the
   round-off of the next paragraph, so a split column and one block take the same branch on a flat profile, where the
   two bounds coincide.

*Round-off.* The interior filter weights are multiples of $1/16$ and exact in binary; `apply` sums five products, so by
the standard dot-product bound $(\mathsf F\chi)_i$ is off by at most $5\epsilon_{\mathrm m}\sum_l\lvert\mathsf F_l\rvert\max\chi
=\tfrac{25}{4}\epsilon_{\mathrm m}\max\chi$, $1.4\times10^{-15}\max\chi$ in double, plus one rounding for the product with
$p_{\mathrm{ref}}$. The face weights are computed in double by `lagrange_deriv`, so they carry a rounding of their own
that is not bounded here; their four-term sum adds at most $4\epsilon_{\mathrm m}\sum_l\lvert a_l\rvert\max\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}
=\tfrac{16}{3}\epsilon_{\mathrm m}\max\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}$ in the interior, with $\sum_l\lvert a_l\rvert=16/12$ for the
weights $a_l=(-1,7,7,-1)/12$. The $n_1=256$ level of `[C14]`, at round-off level, lies inside both.

*Exact and truncated.* Exact: the end-cell identity, the face weights for cubics, @eq-ch05-wbref4-pnu for cubics.
$O(\Delta x_1^4)$: $\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}$ and $\eta_{\rho,f}$ in the interior. At the three faces next to a wall the note
gives $O(\Delta x_1^3)$ (the anchor constant through the even ghosts); not re-checked here.

### Numerical method

The stencils are shown in @fig-ch05-wbref4-stencils. The stencils and weights are built once per block, on the CPU in double
precision, and cached until device or dtype changes; application is a gather and a weighted sum on the block's device.
The cell part runs right after the kernel in `_hydro_ref_x1`, before the seam ghost-row exchange; the face part runs
after it, so a column split along $x_1$ gets the same faces as one block. A block with a clamped wall and fewer than
four owned cells keeps the kernel's reference.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch05-wbref4-stencils
#| fig-cap: "The `SNAP_WB_REF4` stencils at a bottom wall (thick black line), $x_1$ to the right. Top: the filter $\\mathsf F$ on the wall cell $i_s$ reads two values past the wall (bluish-green diamonds $E_1$, $E_2$), which are cubic extrapolations of the four owned cells nearest it (sky-blue circles), never the hatched ghosts; with them the filtered ratio equals $\\chi$ in the end cell. Bottom: the face density at the wall face from the quartic primitive over the four owned cells next to the wall (orange triangles at the five faces); interior faces use the centred weights $(-1, 7, 7, -1)/12$."
#| fig-alt: "Two rows of cells beside a wall with hatched ghosts; in the top row diamonds sit in two ghost cells and circles in four interior cells under a bracket of five cells; in the bottom row triangles mark five faces under a bracket of four cells."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch05.figures.fig_wbref4_stencils import make_fig
make_fig()
```

**The oracle and the measured order.** The test drives a neutral polytrope ($\gamma=5/3$, $g=n_{\mathrm{poly}}+1$ with
the polytropic index $n_{\mathrm{poly}}=1/(\gamma-1)$, $T_0=1+L_z-z$) seeded with a divergence-free overturning mode of amplitude $10^{-4}$, takes one RK3[^rg-5ce8343548de]
step, and measures $N^2_{\mathrm{eff}}=\tfrac g\gamma\sum_i(-\mathcal S_i)v_{1,i}/\sum_iv_{1,i}^2$ from the entropy tendency $\mathcal S_i$ of
the mode minus that of the rest state. For this column the exact cell-average tendencies vanish at linear order, so every
$N^2_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is scheme error. @fig-ch05-wbref4-order shows the four arms at the pin.[^ch05-wb4-fig]

[^ch05-wb4-fig]: Data `src/snapy_report/ch05/data/wb_ref4_order.json`, from `python tests/test_wb_ref4_order.py` (from the
    build's `tests` directory, `PYTHONPATH` set to this build's Python package) against a CPU Release build of snapy@6fbb39750f62b83df096058a4746e77d0a634bc5 (snapy 2.11.10.dev1+g6fbb397, torch 2.10.0+cu128, kintera 2.6.2.dev4+g914389b40), 2026-10-12, double, 1 rank; the
    `SNAP_GRAVITY_WORK_RADIAL_EXACT=0` arms from a second run with that variable set. The test sets
    `SNAP_FLUX_COVARIANCE=1` itself, so the default of that switch does not enter.

```{python}

Vermillion circles: `SNAP_WB_REF4` off; bluish-green squares: on. Solid lines: the corrected-PE face work at its default (on); dotted lines with open markers: `SNAP_GRAVITY_WORK_RADIAL_EXACT=0`. A flat line is second-order convergence of $N^2_{\\mathrm{eff}}$; the black dotted guide has slope $-2$, i.e. fourth order. #| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch05.figures.fig_wbref4_order import make_fig
```

At the pin, with the corrected-PE face work at its default, the observed orders of $\lvert N^2_{\mathrm{eff}}\rvert$
are 4.07, 4.03 (1 e-fold) and 3.88, 3.94 (3 e-folds) with the switch, and 2.13, 2.04 and 2.21, 2.08 without it. With
`SNAP_GRAVITY_WORK_RADIAL_EXACT=0` the switched arm returns 2.96, 2.98 and 2.84, 2.92, and its values
$-0.0707$, $-0.0358$ (1 e-fold, $n_1$ = 64, 128) and $-0.2257$, $-0.1194$ (3 e-folds) equal the table of the
derivation note to the printed digits.[^ch05-wb4-tab] The order-3 "wall band" that note leaves unidentified is
therefore removed by the corrected-PE face work, tested by switching that work off and on with everything else fixed,
not derived.

### Code

**A minimal input.** The switch is an environment variable, not a YAML key. A deck it acts on needs gravity along
$x_1$, three ghost cells and, for the wall stencils, the wall clamp:

```yaml
geometry:
  type: cartesian
  bounds: {x1min: 0., x1max: 1.e4}
  cells: {nx1: 64, nghost: 3}   # three ghost cells: the setup check below
dynamics:
  wb-wall-clamp: true           # the default; the wall stencils use owned cells only
forcing:
  const-gravity: {grav1: -9.8}
```

With these keys in a copy of `straka_single.yaml`, saved as `deck.yaml` in `build/bin` of a build at the pin
([Install and run](#sec-preface-install)), run

```bash
SNAP_WB_REF4=1 ./straka.release deck.yaml
```

A PyPI release of snapy has no such switch and ignores the variable without a message.

**What it refuses, and why.** Setup refuses $n_g<3$ with gravity on
({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}), because the flag of step 3 above would then read
cells a block does not hold, and the two sides of a seam could disagree. Values of `SNAP_WB_REF4` other than empty,
`0`, `false`, `off` or `no` (any case) turn it on. A block with a clamped wall and fewer than four owned cells, or with
fewer than five cells in all, is not refused: its stencils are marked unusable
({{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_stencils >}}) and it keeps the kernel's reference.

**The lines that implement @eq-ch05-wbref4-dref and @eq-ch05-wbref4-face.** From `wb_ref4_cells` and
`wb_ref4_faces`:

```cpp
auto r = w[IDN] / w[IPR];
auto fr = apply(r, st.fidx, st.fwt);
...
dref.narrow(-1, st.is, nown)
    .copy_(torch::where(fl, d_old, torch::where(ok, p_new * fr, keep)));
...
auto face = apply(dref, st.aidx, st.awt);
...
d.copy_(torch::where(ok, face, d));
```

`r` is $\chi$, `fr` is $\mathsf F\chi$ and `p_new * fr` the first line of @eq-ch05-wbref4-dref; `fl` is the dilated
flag, which keeps the kernel's `d_old`, and `ok` the range guard, which keeps `keep`: `d_old` on a uniform grid and
`p_new * (d_old / p_old)` otherwise ({{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_cells >}}). `face` is $\partial_1\Pi(x_{1,f})$ of
@eq-ch05-wbref4-face with the weights `awt`, written to $\rho_{\mathrm{sf}}$ (`d`) where its own guard passes.

|--------|----------|----------|------|
| the switch, implied by the centroid switch | {{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_enabled >}} | `wb_ref4_enabled` | `SNAP_WB_REF4` |
| margin and resolution threshold | {{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp kMaxLogDrop >}} | `kMaxLogDrop`, `kMargin` | |
| stencils and weights | {{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_stencils >}} | `wb_ref4_stencils` | |
| cell part and flag | {{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_cells >}} | `wb_ref4_cells` | |
| face part | {{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_faces >}} | `wb_ref4_faces` | |
| ghost-depth check | {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}} | `wb_ref4_enabled` | $n_g\ge3$ |
| calls around the seam exchange | {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::_hydro_ref_x1 >}} | `wb_ref4_cells` | |

: Code map of `SNAP_WB_REF4`. {#tbl-ch05-wbref4-code}

1. `wb_ref4_enabled` reads the environment once; values other than empty, `0`, `false`, `off`, `no` turn it on, and
   `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` turns it on too
   ({{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_enabled >}}).
2. At setup, with gravity on, $n_g<3$ fails the `TORCH_CHECK` that names `wb_ref4_enabled`
   ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}).
3. In `_hydro_ref_x1` the stencils are built once per block and `wb_ref4_cells` replaces $\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}$ (and on a
   non-uniform grid $p_{\mathrm{ref}}$) and returns the resolution flag
   ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::_hydro_ref_x1 >}}).
4. After the seam exchange `wb_ref4_faces` replaces $\rho_{\mathrm{sf}}$
   ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::_hydro_ref_x1 >}}).

The only user-facing error is the ghost-depth check of step 2.

: Tests of `SNAP_WB_REF4`. {#tbl-ch05-wbref4-tests}

`[C3]` confirms the moments of $\mathsf F$ (unit sum, zero first to third, fourth $-\tfrac32$) and its zero response at
the two-cell mode, $\vartheta=\pi/2$. `[C7]` confirms the two cubic wall rows and that the two end cells keep $\chi$ exactly. `[C8]`
derives the three face rows, interior, wall and next, in exact rationals. `[C14]` measures the face offset quoted in
the Derivation, order 2.00 for the kernel and about 6 with the switch until round-off.

::: {.callout-important title="Test"}
**Evidence.** Check numbers come from `wbref_check.py` (`[C3]`, `[C7]`, `[C8]`, `[C14]`).[^ch05-wb4-chk] At the pin
$N^2_{\mathrm{eff}}n_1^2$ at $n_1$ = 32, 64, 128 is, switch off, $+0.0719$, $+0.0656$, $+0.0640$ (1 e-fold) and
$+0.6198$, $+0.5344$, $+0.5060$ (3 e-folds); on, $+0.0025$, $+0.0006$, $+0.0001$ and $+0.0407$, $+0.0111$, $+0.0029$
(@fig-ch05-wbref4-order). The seam tests print gaps of $6.775\times10^{-15}$ and $1.675\times10^{-15}$ ($\alpha_{\mathrm{nh}}$ = 1, 0)
for the split and 0 for two ranks against two blocks, and every ctest entry of the table passes.[^ch05-wb4-run]
**Coverage.** CPU; the CUDA twin `test_wb_ref4_order_cuda` and the `_cuda` seam arms were not run (**pending: a CUDA
run at the pin**); 2 ranks through the `_mp` arm.

[^ch05-wb4-run]: `python tests/test_wb_ref4_order.py` as in the figure note, and
    `ctest -V -R 'test_wb_ref4_order|test_x1_seam_split|test_balance_column_wb_ref4|test_face_floor_wb_ref4'` in the build directory of
    a CPU Release build of snapy@6fbb39750f62b83df096058a4746e77d0a634bc5 (snapy 2.11.10.dev1+g6fbb397, torch 2.10.0+cu128, kintera 2.6.2.dev4+g914389b40), 2026-10-12, double; 1 rank, the `_mp` entries 2 ranks. The ctest entry `test_wb_ref4_order_python` imports this build's
    package through `SNAPY_TEST_PYTHONPATH`.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
`SNAP_WB_REF4` needs `nghost` $\ge3$. It is read once per process, so every block of a run makes the same choice.
:::

1. **Thresholds not derived.** The $0.5$ resolution threshold, the two-cell dilation and the $10^{-10}$ margin are
   design choices.[^ch05-wb4-thr]
2. **Untested.** Stretched-grid dynamics (only `balance_column` exercises the non-uniform branch),
   multi-species columns, and seams across more than two ranks.
3. **Resolution of the order test.** The test grid is $n_1$ = 32/64/128 against 64/128/256 in the note's table, and the
   threshold `ORDER_ON` 2.75 does not distinguish the fourth order measured at the pin from the third order of the
   note; the test still separates on from off.
4. **Names.** The specification calls the switch `SNAPY_WB_REF_EXACT`; the code reads `SNAP_WB_REF4`.
5. **Untested combinations.** See the switch coverage matrix, @sec-ch12-matrix.
